sentences.text: Ankonetta was an extinct genus of birds belonging to the duck family, Anatidae.
This animal was a mid-sized member of its group.
The holotype fossil — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in the Santa Cruz Formation of Argentina.
The genus name honors the Aónikenk people of Patagonia, while the species name commemorates researcher Claudio Larriestra.
The genus was described by Cenizo and Agnolín in 2010, with Ankonetta larriestrai serving as the type species.
Fossils of Ankonetta date to the Early Miocene epoch, a time between 23.04 and 15.98 million years ago.
